reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the first three premises regarding CSRO effects on hardness, stiffness, plastic zone size, and slow dislocation migration. However, it provides no evidence for thermal expansion mismatch, internal stresses, or their role in unifying creep, hardening, and elastic responses, leaving the core mechanistic premises unsupported.
premises: Chemical short-range order (CSRO) makes HfNbTaTiZr stiffer and harder
CSRO increases plastic zone size and dislocation density during nanoindentation
Slow dislocation migration explains nanoindentation features in HfNbTaTiZr
Thermal expansion mismatch between chemically heterogeneous regions creates internal stresses
These internal stresses impede dislocation motion and unify creep, hardening, and elastic responses
